# muxt test --output-cover-profile writes every block of the package's
# template files as a Go cover profile, count 1 for a block the tests reached
# and 0 for one they did not, and go tool cover -html opens it.
#
# The template file starts with its {{if}}, so the first span starts at the
# file's first byte: the profile counts line 1 from column 2, which is how
# x/tools' cover.Boundaries reads it. The test renders the admin branch
# only, so go tool cover shows the {{else}} branch as uncovered.

muxt test --output-cover-profile cover.out
stdout '^ok  \tserver\t'
cmpenv cover.out want-cover.txt

exec go tool cover -html=cover.out -o out.html
grep '<span class="cov8" title="1">\{\{if \.Admin\}\}</span><span class="cov8" title="1">Welcome back, admin\.</span><span class="cov0" title="0">\{\{else\}\}</span><span class="cov0" title="0">Please sign in\.</span><span class="cov8" title="1">\{\{end\}\}</span>' out.html

-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- index.gohtml --
{{if .Admin}}Welcome back, admin.{{else}}Please sign in.{{end}}
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"embed"
	"html/template"
	"io"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templateFiles embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.ParseFS(templateFiles, "*.gohtml"))

type Page struct {
	Admin bool
}

func Render(w io.Writer, page Page) error {
	return templates.ExecuteTemplate(w, "index.gohtml", page)
}
-- render_test.go --
package server

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestAdminPage(t *testing.T) {
	var buf strings.Builder
	if err := Render(&buf, Page{Admin: true}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got, want := buf.String(), "Welcome back, admin.\n"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("page = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}
-- want-cover.txt --
mode: set
$WORK/index.gohtml:1.2,1.15 1 1
$WORK/index.gohtml:1.15,1.35 1 1
$WORK/index.gohtml:1.35,1.43 1 0
$WORK/index.gohtml:1.43,1.58 1 0
$WORK/index.gohtml:1.58,1.65 1 1
$WORK/index.gohtml:1.65,2.1 1 1
